vts_name: VTS costeiro do continente (Coast of Portugal VTS; call sign 'Roca Control')
vts_authority: Direção-Geral de Recursos Naturais, Segurança e Serviços Marítimos (DGRM); DL 263/2009 names IPTM, I.P. (predecessor)
vts_centre: Centro de Controlo de Tráfego Marítimo do Continente (CCTMC), Paço de Arcos
vts_boundary_basis: Statutory area, DL 263/2009 art. 6 (west/south limit 41 51 05 N 010 14 W, 38 41 N 010 14 W, 36 30 N 009 35 W, 36 12 N 007 24 W); art. 10(4) gives the CCTMC supervision of TSS rules. Pass 4 overlay (Mercator, rhumb-line legs) of COLREG.2/Circ.55 annex 6 positions (ED50): separation zones, inshore traffic zone and all lanes except the outermost southbound (dangerous cargo) lane lie inside. That lane's outer line crosses the limit in two places: positions (35) 36 44.37 N 009 39.59 W and (36) 36 56.72 N 009 43.16 W lie about 0.25 to 0.3 NM west of the western leg, and position (33) 36 25.15 N 009 05.87 W lies about 0.85 NM south of the southern leg (limit at about 36 26.0 N on that meridian). Coverage is therefore partial, by thin edge slivers only.
reporting_scheme_name: COPREP (Off the coast of Portugal); also WETREP (tanker-only)
reporting_authority: Roca Control (CCTMC, DGRM) for COPREP; WETREP via its coastal authorities
reporting_boundary_basis: COPREP (MSC.278(85)): TSS not named. Western leg identical to the VTS limit (38 41 N 010 14 W to 36 30 N 009 35 W), so positions (35) and (36) lie about 0.25 to 0.3 NM outside; the COPREP southern leg (36 30 N 009 35 W to 36 15 N 008 30 W) lies further south than the VTS leg, so position (33) is inside COPREP. All of the TSS except that western sliver is inside. COPREP applies to ships 300 GT+, dangerous/polluting cargo, passenger ships, fishing vessels 24 m+, tows over 100 m. WETREP (MSC.190(79)) names 'Off Cape S. Vicente' in para 6.2.1; applies only to oil tankers over 600 dwt carrying heavy grades (decision 2).
evidence_summary: Portuguese coastal VTS (VTS-0023, Roca Control) statutory area and COPREP area share the western limit line; overlay of the 2005 amended TSS shows the scheme inside apart from edge slivers of the outermost southbound lane (about 0.3 NM on the west; about 0.85 NM at the south-east end for the VTS area only). DGRM pages (live, accessed 30 Sep 2026) confirm the coastal VTS and Roca Control are current. WETREP names the TSS.
source_date: DL 263/2009 (28 Sep 2009); MSC.278(85) (1 Dec 2008); COLREG.2/Circ.55 (15 Dec 2004); DGRM pages accessed 2026-09-30
unresolved_issue: Overlay used the 2005 ED50 coordinates from COLREG.2/Circ.55 (ED50 to WGS84 shift of roughly 0.1 NM not applied); the Ships' Routeing 2025 description was not opened. DL 263/2009 checked as published; later amendments to art. 6 not checked. 'Partial' reflects edge slivers only; the TSS is practically within the Roca Control service.
vts_coverage_type: Partial TSS coverage; see boundary basis
review_note: Stage 2 association review (four-pass audit), 2026-09-30. First-pass lead: confirmed (VTS + MRS, VTS-0023, VRS-0012), with coordinate overlay added, extent recorded as partial by about 0.3 NM, and WETREP (VRS-0005) added. Pass 4: CONFIRMED VTS + MRS (VTS-0023; COPREP VRS-0012; WETREP VRS-0005). 'Partial' kept: re-running the overlay shows the outermost southbound lane outside the VTS limit by about 0.3 NM on the west and also about 0.85 NM at its south-east end (position 33, missed by the researcher, but inside COPREP); basis text corrected.

source_date: MSC.300(87) (17 May 2010, in force 1 Dec 2010); Tramos Feb 2025; SASEMAR Plan de Actuación 2025-2027 and Plan Anual 2025 (posted 8 Oct 2025)

vts_name: Salvamento Marítimo traffic service for the Cabo de Gata DST (CCS Almería); radio call sign not verified

vts_centre: Centro de Coordinación de Salvamento (CCS) Almería
vts_boundary_basis: Named: the SASEMAR Plan de Actuación 2025-2027 and Plan Anual 2025 (ministerial orders, Oct 2025) assign CCS Almería the supervision of maritime traffic in the Cabo de Gata DST; the official SASEMAR site states Salvamento Marítimo provides traffic monitoring and assistance ('seguimiento y ayuda al tráfico') in the DST of Finisterre, Tarifa, Cabo de Gata and Canarias; Tramos (Feb 2025) states Spanish DST are controlled by VTS (STM), a function assigned to Salvamento Marítimo. reporting_boundary_basis: No Part I system (baseline list). Spanish official statement: reporting at Cabo de Gata is voluntary; IMO circular note provides voluntary notification only.
evidence_summary: 2025 ministerial orders name CCS Almería as supervising traffic in the Cabo de Gata DST; the official SASEMAR site lists Cabo de Gata among the DST where it monitors and assists traffic; CCS Almería is an operating VTS centre (Almería Port Control). Reporting is voluntary only.
source_date: SASEMAR Plan de Actuación 2025-2027 and Plan Anual 2025 (posted 8 Oct 2025); Tramos Feb 2025; COLREG.2/Circ.57 (26 May 2006)
unresolved_issue: No official source gives a distinct service name or VHF call sign for the Cabo de Gata DST traffic service (unlike 'Tarifa Traffic' and the Finisterre STM); the only IMO text (COLREG.2/Circ.57) refers to Almería MRCC for voluntary notification.

tss_name: In the Adriatic Sea: in the North Adriatic Sea
vts_authority: Ministarstvo mora, prometa i infrastrukture (Ministry of the Sea, Transport and Infrastructure), Croatia
vts_centre: VTS centres named in MSC.598(111): Rijeka, Split, Dubrovnik
vts_sector: Probably surveillance Sector A (NN 52/2025 art. 102); sector boundaries are in an image annex not read
vts_boundary_basis: NN 52/2025 art. 93(12): the VTS area covers Croatian internal waters, territorial sea and exclusive economic zone; art. 101(2): the VTS service supervises the IMO-adopted routeing and TSS in the Adriatic. Pass 4 overlay against the 1968 Italy-Yugoslavia continental shelf line (points 7 to 17), which Croatia's EEZ limit towards Italy follows: every vertex of the eastern part (positions 4a-4d, 5a-5b, 6a-6b) lies about 6 to 17 NM east of the line, i.e. on the Croatian side; the western part lies mainly on the Italian side (separation zone and southbound lane 3 to 13 NM west), with only the outer edge of its northbound lane (9a, 9b) about 0.6 to 0.8 NM east of the line. IMO structure (COLREG.2/Circ.54 annex 3; HHI notice 11/2004) groups the eastern and western parts under 'In the North Adriatic Sea', with the approaches to the Gulfs of Trieste and Venice as separate schemes (B-III/9, B-III/10), consistent with B-III/8 comprising both parts. The Venice VTS users' manual states the North Adriatic TSS is not inside the Venice VTS area.
reporting_authority: Until 30 Nov 2026 (MSC.139(76)): sector 4 Ancona MRSC, sector 5 Venezia MRSC / Trieste MRSC / Koper MRCC. From 1 Dec 2026 (MSC.598(111)): electronic reporting via SafeSeaNet with shore authorities including VTS Croatia, VTS Venezia, VTS Trieste, Ravenna and Ancona Coast Guard, MRCC Koper
reporting_boundary_basis: Area: whole Adriatic north of 40 25 N (both resolutions); TSS lies between about 43 53 N and 44 57 N, inside. Applicability now: oil tankers 150 GT+, ships 300 GT+ with dangerous or polluting goods. From 0000 UTC 1 Dec 2026: oil tankers 150 GT+, all ships 10,000 GT+, all other ships carrying hazardous cargo.
evidence_summary: Inside ADRIREP by area. Croatian 2025 regulation extends the VTS area to the Croatian EEZ and gives the VTS service supervision of the IMO Adriatic TSS; overlay against the Italy-Croatia shelf line puts the whole eastern part of the North Adriatic TSS on the Croatian side. The western part is mainly on the Italian side and outside the Venice VTS area; Italian VTS coverage of it not established. VTS partial.
unresolved_issue: (1) Ships' Routeing 2025 text of B-III/8 not opened; composition (eastern and western parts) inferred from COLREG.2/Circ.54 and the register numbering. (2) Croatian EEZ decision and 2005 technical correction of the shelf line not opened; Sector A limits (NN 52/2025 annex 4 image) not overlaid; datum differences (ED50/Hermannskogel) not applied, immaterial at 6 NM or more. (3) Italian coverage of the western part (Ravenna/Ancona Coast Guard) not established.
vts_coverage_type: Partial TSS coverage; see boundary basis
review_note: Stage 2 association review (four-pass audit), 2026-09-30. First-pass lead: corrected: MRS only to VTS + MRS (VTS Croatia, partial, NN 52/2025); ADRIREP VRS-0015 confirmed with both regimes recorded. Leads only: VTS Venezia, Ravenna Coast Guard, Ancona Coast Guard (Italy; ADRIREP authorities, TSS coverage not shown); Koper VTS and VTS Trieste relate to the Gulf of Trieste (B22). Pass 4: CONFIRMED VTS + MRS, VTS partial. Overlay against the 1968 Italy-Yugoslavia shelf line puts the whole eastern part 6 to 17 NM inside Croatian jurisdiction; COLREG.2/Circ.54 and the register numbering support B-III/8 comprising both parts. The western part is outside the Venice VTS area (Venice VTS manual); Ships' Routeing 2025 text still to be checked.

Scheme is outside the VTS Trieste (westernmost 013°34.6'E), Koper and Venice VTS areas (SRC-2032, SRC-2029, SRC-2033).

reporting_boundary_basis: ADRIREP (VRS-0015): whole Adriatic north of 40°25'N (MSC.598(111) para 2.1; current Part I text MSC.139(76) in force until 30 Nov 2026, revised system from 1 Dec 2026, same area).
evidence_summary: Inside ADRIREP (VRS-0015). The official Croatian VTS area dataset (revised March 2025, served live 30 Sep 2026) places most of the scheme in VTS Croatia Sector A (Croatian EEZ surveillance sector); VTS Croatia is named as an ADRIREP shore-based authority in MSC.598(111) (May 2026), confirming current operation. Coordinates place the scheme outside the Trieste, Koper and Venice VTS areas.
source_date: MSC.598(111) 22 May 2026; Circ.54 28 May 2004; Koper manual 30 Nov 2025; Trieste manual Jan 2018
unresolved_issue: None for classification. Overlap measured from dataset geometry against COLREG.2/Circ.54 lane limits; Sector A offers information service on request only (no traffic organisation service).

review_note: Stage 2 association review (four-pass audit), 2026-09-30. Pass 4 changed the classification: CORRECTED: MRS only to VTS + MRS (partial). The researcher's VTS Croatia lead is resolved by the official Croatian VTS dataset (revised March 2025): about 77% of the scheme lies in Sector A; VTS Croatia is confirmed current by MSC.598(111). tss_name: In the Adriatic Sea: approaches to Gulf of Venice
reporting_scheme_name: ADRIREP (In the Adriatic Sea), IMO Part I I-I/15
reporting_authority: Venice MRSC under MSC.139(76); VTS Venezia under MSC.598(111) from 1 Dec 2026; other Adriatic shore-based authorities
reporting_boundary_basis: ADRIREP (VRS-0015): whole Adriatic north of 40°25'N (MSC.598(111) para 2.1; current Part I text MSC.139(76) in force until 30 Nov 2026, revised system from 1 Dec 2026, same area).
evidence_summary: ADRIREP applies. Venice VTS (operational, on the national list of 11 centres) does not cover this TSS: its own manual lists the IMO scheme as outside the VTS area, and coordinates show it ends about 1 nm outside the outer limit. Vessels must call Venice VTS 5 NM before the outer limit, which may fall inside the TSS, but this is a first-call point, not evidence of monitoring the scheme.
source_date: Venice manual last updated 19/09/2017 (current portal edition); Circ.58 11 Dec 2006; MSC.598(111) 22 May 2026
unresolved_issue: None for classification. Whether Venice VTS monitors the scheme outside its area (decision 1) has no official evidence.
review_note: Stage 2 association review (four-pass audit), 2026-09-30. First-pass lead: confirmed: MRS only; first-pass audit claim that the Venice manual places this TSS in the VTS area corrected (that is a local scheme; the IMO scheme is in Annex 4, outside). Leads only: Venice VTS (Guardia Costiera, Capitaneria di Porto di Venezia): adjoining; first call 5 NM outside outer limit. Pass 4: CONFIRMED: MRS only. Venice manual (current portal edition) puts the Circ.58 scheme in Annex 4 'outside Venice V.T.S. area' and says 'Even if not inside Venice VTS Area'; the northern lane ends lie about 0.6 to 0.8 nm outside line B-C; no Croatian VTS polygon reaches it. ADRIREP confirmed.

vts_centre: Koper VTS (call sign Koper VTS, VHF 69, backup 72)

tss_name: In the southern approaches to the Kerch Strait
vts_boundary_basis: Not established. Rosmorport publishes a Kerch Strait VTS area (Compulsory Regulations of Kavkaz, Order No. 110 of 23.03.2018, and Taman, Order No. 16 of 22.01.2014) whose southern limit is 44°59.75'N between 36°27.26'E and 36°41.60'E. The UKHO Black Sea Pilot (NP 24, 2003, lead only) places the south end of the TSS at 44°50'N 36°30'E, about 10 NM south of that limit, so at most part of the TSS could fall inside the claimed polygon. The area is disputed; the Rosmorport claim is recorded as one party's statement only, and no current Ukrainian operational source was found.
reporting_boundary_basis: No IMO Part I system covers the area (SRC-2048). The compulsory reports to Kerch Strait VTS described by Rosmorport are routine VTS reporting, not a separate MRS. No other scheme was identified.
evidence_summary: Rosmorport, a Russian Federation operator, publishes a Kerch Strait VTS (Kavkaz centre, Kerch sub-centre) whose area polygon has a southern limit of 44°59.75'N. Whether the IMO TSS falls inside is not shown. The area is disputed: Ukraine's position, including its communications to IMO (e.g. Circular Letter 4508, not opened in this pass), is recorded neutrally. Nothing here is evidence of current safe operation.
source_date: Rosmorport page undated (cites Order No. 16 of 22.01.2014)
unresolved_issue: Overlay the current IMO B-III/15 TSS coordinates on the claimed polygon (the 2003 NP 24 lead suggests the TSS extends south of it, so partial at most). Project decision needed on how to record services claimed by an operator whose jurisdiction in this area is disputed. The IMO Circular Letter 4508 text was not retrieved.
review_note: Stage 2 association review (four-pass audit), 2026-09-30. First-pass lead: confirmed: kept Unresolved with no operator assigned. Refined with the published polygon southern limit.. Leads only: Kerch Strait VTS (Rosmorport claim; disputed). Historical Ukrainian Kerch VTS (pre-2014), historical only.. Pass 4: CONFIRMED Unresolved (spot-check). A 2003 UKHO Pilot lead puts the TSS south end at 44°50'N, south of the claimed 44°59.75'N limit, so at most partial; recorded neutrally, disputed area.

vts_name: Türk Boğazları Gemi Trafik Hizmetleri (TBGTH) / Turkish Straits Vessel Traffic Service (TSVTS)
vts_authority: Kıyı Emniyeti Genel Müdürlüğü (Directorate General of Coastal Safety), operating for the Ministry of Transport and Infrastructure (Administration)
vts_centre: İstanbul VTS Centre (İstinye) and Çanakkale VTS Centre (Akbaş)
vts_sector: Sector names and limits not verified from a current official source (the TSVTS User's Guide was not obtained). First-pass sector names are leads only. First-pass lead: Sector Türkeli (VHF 11).
vts_boundary_basis: Statutory. Art. 5 of the 2019 Regulation establishes TBGTH 'for the implementation and supervision of the traffic separation scheme and the operation of the reporting system'. Art. 4(2) of the 2019 Regulation sets the limits of the Turkish Straits TSS: north line 41°20.944'N between 028°54.974'E and 029°15.974'E; south line through 40°01.940'N 25°54.970'E, 39°49.940'N 25°52.970'E and 39°43.940'N 25°54.970'E to 26°09.129'E. All Annex 1.1 'İstanbul Boğazı Kuzey Yaklaşması' points (41°13.303'N to 41°20.443'N, 029°01.974'E to 029°15.974'E) lie inside that northern limit. TÜBRAP SP-2 (2 h or 20 NM) and position reports (5 NM before entry) go to the TBGTH Centre on this approach. No VTS sector chart obtained.
reporting_scheme_name: TÜBRAP (Türk Boğazları Rapor Sistemi / Turkish Straits Reporting System), national scheme under the Turkish Straits Maritime Traffic Regulation 2019 (not IMO Part I)
reporting_authority: Ministry of Transport and Infrastructure (Administration); reports made to the TBGTH Centres (Istanbul and Çanakkale), operated by KEGM
reporting_boundary_basis: Art. 7 TÜBRAP reports are made to the TBGTH Centre before and on entry to the Istanbul Strait from the north (SP-2 2 h or 20 NM before entry; position report 5 NM before entry), so they apply to ships using the north approach TSS. Applicability: SP-1 for ships carrying dangerous cargo and ships of 500 GT and above (24 h before entering the Istanbul or Çanakkale Strait, or 6 h before departure from Marmara ports); SP-2 by VHF 2 h or 20 NM before strait entry; position report by ships of 20 m and above 5 NM before strait entry; calling-point reports in the straits; MARRAP for active participants using the TBGTH area in the Sea of Marmara. Applies to all flags. Counted as MRS under project decision 3.
evidence_summary: The 2019 Regulation names the north approach TSS (Annex 1.1) as part of the Turkish Straits TSS that TBGTH is established to implement and supervise (Art. 5). The 2023 Implementation Directive confirms TBGTH Centres are current. TÜBRAP (national) applies on this approach. No VTS sector polygon was obtained, so coverage rests on the statutory link and the approach reporting duties.
source_date: Regulation 15/08/2019 (consolidated to 16/12/2020); Implementation Directive 04.12.2023 (in force 01.01.2024); KEGM pages undated
unresolved_issue: The TSVTS User's Guide sector limits (seaward limit of the Istanbul VTS area in the north approach) were not obtained. Coverage is recorded as full on the statutory basis; confirm with the sector chart.
vts_coverage_type: Full TSS coverage by the recorded service
review_note: Stage 2 association review (four-pass audit), 2026-09-30. First-pass lead: corrected: VTS confirmed from statutory sources (Art. 5 and Annex 1.1), not the user guide. Sector Türkeli is unverified. TÜBRAP confirmed absent from the project Part I baseline and counted as a national MRS.. Pass 4: CONFIRMED VTS + MRS. TÜBRAP SP-2 and 5 NM position reports fall on this approach; full coverage rests on the statutory link, sector chart still not obtained.

vts_authority: Saudi Aramco (Manager, Port Operations, Port of Ras Tanura)
vts_centre: Ras Tanura Port Control (Ras Tanura Port Control Center)
vts_boundary_basis: Aramco July 2025 book: the VTMS is mandatory 'for all vessels within the Port of Ras Tanura'. The 11-point harbour boundary has its eastern limit on 50 23 E between 27 00 N and 27 12 N. The IMO scheme (A.338(IX) as amended) runs from 50 42 E west to the Ras Tanura channel at about 26 41 N 50 12 E. The Ju'aymah departure lane (Part III) runs east along 27 11.5 N to 50 36 E. Inside the port limits: the channel section, the Ju'aymah approach lane and the western end of the departure lane. Outside them: the eastern approach lanes (about 50 23 E to 50 42 E) and the eastern part of the Ju'aymah departure lane (50 23 E to 50 36 E). Pub. 172 (2025) lists VTMS reporting to Ras Tannurah Port Control from Ras Tannurah Lighted Buoy (27 06 N 50 57 E), east of the scheme, and the Aramco speed rules apply to all ships 'using the Ras Tanura Port, Traffic Separation Scheme' from the Approach Buoy. So traffic in the whole scheme is in contact with the service. The service's defined area is still the port. Hence partial. The service is a VTS in its own right: it is a mandatory VTMS with a 'VTS Operator' information service, so the decision 5 fallback is not needed.
reporting_boundary_basis: Not in IMO Part I. Reports to Ras Tanura Port Control (Entry buoy, A buoy, anchoring, departure) are routine VTMS reporting and form part of the VTS, not a separate MRS. No national mandatory reporting scheme found in Pub. 172 (2025) or the Aramco book.
evidence_summary: Aramco's July 2025 port book describes a mandatory VTMS with a 'VTS Operator' information service. It covers all vessels within the Port of Ras Tanura and states that the Ras Tanura Channel separation zones and routes are IMO-approved. Speed and reporting rules apply to 'all ships using the Ras Tanura Port, Traffic Separation Scheme'. The port boundary includes the channel and Ju'aymah parts of the TSS but not the eastern approach lanes between about 50 23 E and 50 42 E. Pub. 172 (2025) confirms the VTMS covers Ras Tannurah and the Ju Aymah terminals and lists reporting points along the approach. It is an official port traffic management service (decision 5), with partial coverage.
source_date: Aramco Ports and Terminals July 2025; NGA Pub. 172 24th ed. 2025; IMO A.338(IX) 1975
